signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Unwind
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades under heavy pressure as JPY emerges as the clear G10 leader with a 1W average outperformance of +2.104%. The spread between the leading JPY and the laggard CAD has widened to 2.955%, a critical threshold indicating a powerful bilateral theme. Despite a +125bp OIS carry advantage for the CAD (CORRA 2.31% vs TONA 0.98%), the pair is being liquidated as oil prices collapse over 5% on Iran diplomacy hopes. JPY strength is further supported by a positive ESI of +22.9, contrasting with the deteriorating risk sentiment signaled by the 0.94% drop in the Nikkei. The bear steepener regime in US yields typically precedes late-cycle volatility, favoring the JPY's return as a funding currency being covered. Risk: A reversal in oil prices or a hawkish BoC surprise that restores the carry appeal of CAD.

signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Scorecard + Options Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 157.04 is trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (162.34/161.31/157.95), confirming a technical breakdown. The options market is aggressively positioning for further downside with a strong 25d risk reversal of -2.53, even as the OIS carry differential remains wide at +267bp in favor of the USD. This negative VRP of -1.7% suggests IV (7.2%) is lagging realized volatility (8.9%), indicating that the recent move lower has caught the options market under-hedged. Speculative positioning remains heavily short JPY (LF net -124,575), creating a massive short-squeeze runway if the carry trade continues to flush. Fed's Williams' support for recent policy on a day of Iran-related risk-on sentiment in equities has failed to lift the pair, suggesting JPY-specific demand is dominant. Risk: A sudden spike in US 10Y yields toward 5% that forces a re-engagement of the carry trade.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5868 is holding above its SMA200 at 0.5826 and the SMA20/50 cluster near 0.5795. There is a glaring divergence between speculative positioning (COT LF net short -30,606) and the RBNZ's hawkish stance (RBNZ at 2.5% and actively hiking). This bearish spec bias, represented by a 9.7% long ratio, is being challenged by the strongest Economic Surprise Index in the G10 at +33.4. Retail sentiment is also heavily short (74%), creating a contrarian bullish setup where both retail and institutional specs are positioned against a central bank that is outperforming data expectations. A sustained break above 0.5900 likely triggers a significant short-covering rally toward the 0.6000 handle. Risk: RBNZ softens its tone in the September 2nd meeting, validating the existing spec shorts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + Technical Anchor
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3452, firmly above its SMA cluster (20/50/200 all between 1.3365 and 1.3400). The options market is pricing in a massive volatility risk premium (VRP) of +4.9%, with IV at 11.0% against a realized HV30 of 6.1%. This suggests investors are paying a steep premium for protection, likely due to the upcoming BoE and Fed meetings in mid-September. Speculative positioning is already net long (+36,661), and with OIS carry effectively neutral (-8bp), the pair lacks a clear directional carry driver. The restrictive real rate of +0.93% supports the GBP fundamentally, but the extreme vol premium suggests a breakout move is being anticipated by the desks. Risk: A close below the 1.3365 SMA50 support which would signal a transition from a bullish trend to a range-bound or bearish regime.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme + ESI
signals.text: USD/NOK retail sentiment has reached a 100% long extreme, marking a total capitulation of retail sellers into the recent downtrend. This contrarian signal aligns with the fundamental backdrop as the Norges Bank remains on hold at 4.25% with a market hike bias, while the NOK Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is the strongest in the data set at +34.4. The technical position of USD/NOK below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (9.60-9.71 range) suggests the bearish momentum is structurally intact despite the retail attempt to catch the bottom. A restrictive real rate of +1.51% in Norway provides a fundamental anchor for NOK strength that retail flows are currently fighting. Risk: A sudden recovery in USD/NOK above 9.66 (SMA20) that forces a secondary retail add and stalls the trend.
